age.evidence: Male Sprague-Dawley rats (n = 44; Harlan, Inc., Indianapolis, IN, USA) weighed 225-250 g upon arrival

sex.evidence: Male Sprague-Dawley rats (n = 44; Harlan, Inc., Indianapolis, IN, USA)

dosing.evidence: (-)-DOI hydrochloride (Sigma) was dissolved in 0.9% NaCl... (-)-DOI was administered subcutaneously (s.c.)... dose-response curve of (-)-DOI (0.03, 0.1, 0.3 mg/kg)

handling.evidence: Rats were pairhoused and weighed and handled daily by the experimenter throughout the study.

assays.assay_description: Standard operant chambers, 60-min daily sessions, FR5 schedule for 0.25 mg/kg/inf cocaine. Measures: infusions earned, active lever presses, inactive lever presses, latency to first response. (-)-DOI dose-response tested with/without M100907 pretreatment.

setup_restrain.evidence: Standard operant conditioning chambers with retractable response levers; animals freely moving

food_restriction.evidence: Rats were freely fed with food and water available throughout all phases of the studies, except during operant training sessions.

water_restriction.evidence: Rats were freely fed with food and water available throughout all phases of the studies, except during operant training sessions.

time_to_assay.evidence: Pretreatment times for... (-)-DOI (20 min) were based on previous literature.

sample_size.evidence: Fig. 1 Acute administration of (-)-DOI decreases cocaine (0.25 mg/kg/inf) self-administration (n = 10).

outcomes.summary: Acute (-)-DOI (0.03-0.3 mg/kg, s.c.) dose-dependently reduced cocaine infusions and active lever presses on an FR5 schedule, with no effect on inactive lever presses or latency to first response. M100907 (0.01 mg/kg) partially reversed the suppression of infusions and active lever presses.
outcomes.statistics: Infusions: F(5,45)=27.20, p<0.05; active lever presses: F(5,45)=23.27, p<0.05; inactive lever: F(5,45)=0.27, n.s.; latency: F(5,45)=1.12, n.s.
outcomes.evidence: All doses of (-)-DOI (0.03, 0.1, 0.3 mg/kg) reduced the number of cocaine infusions (p < 0.05) and active lever responses versus VEH (p < 0.05).

B1_num_measures.evidence: cocaine infusions earned, active lever presses, inactive lever presses, and latency to first response

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Totals over 60-min session reported; no within-session time-course analysis

B6_cognitive.evidence: Rats were trained to lever press for cocaine infusions (operant learning)

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med-Associates operant system (beam break/lever press recording)

E8_food_water.evidence: Except during operant training sessions (no food/water in chamber)

D1_continuity.evidence: daily 60-min sessions... Tests were administered in a pseudorandomized order with a minimum of two intervening sessions of cocaine IVSA followed by a VEH test

D3_recording_days.evidence: Training to FR1, FR3, FR5 across multiple sessions followed by pseudorandomized testing of 3 DOI doses + VEH + M100907 combinations with intervening sessions

D4_baseline.evidence: VEH tests preceded each pharmacological challenge and were averaged across days for comparison.

D5_followup.evidence: No follow-up >=24 h after last drug reported

assays.assay_name: Cocaine IVSA Behavioral Economics Threshold Procedure
assays.assay_description: Within-session threshold procedure in standard operant chambers; 180-min sessions; 12 successive 10-min blocks with progressively decreasing cocaine dose per infusion (0.75 to 0.003 mg/kg/inf) on FR3. Demand curve parameters extracted: α, Q0, total intake, Omax, Pmax, EV, load-up intake, latency.

setup_restrain.evidence: Standard operant conditioning chambers; animals freely moving

food_restriction.evidence: Rats were freely fed with food and water available throughout all phases of the studies, except during operant training sessions.

water_restriction.evidence: Rats were freely fed with food and water available throughout all phases of the studies, except during operant training sessions.

time_to_assay.evidence: Pretreatment times for... (-)-DOI (20 min) were based on previous literature.

sample_size.evidence: Fig. 2 Acute administration of (-)-DOI decreases cocaine demand (n = 11).

outcomes.summary: Acute (-)-DOI (0.3 mg/kg) increased demand elasticity (α) and decreased total cocaine consumption, Omax, Pmax, EV, and load-up period intake, indicating devaluation of cocaine reward and reduced motivation. M100907 pretreatment reversed effects on α, total consumption, Omax, and load-up intake but not EV or Pmax.
outcomes.evidence: the dose of 0.3 mg/kg (-)-DOI significantly increased α (p < 0.05) and decreased total cocaine intake during the session (p < 0.05), Omax (p < 0.05), EV (p < 0.05), Pmax (p < 0.05), and cocaine consumption in the first ten minutes (p < 0.05)

B1_num_measures.evidence: demand intensity (Q0), demand elasticity (α), total cocaine consumption, maximum expenditure (Omax), essential value (EV), maximum price-point (Pmax), initial cocaine intake, and latency to first response

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Demand curve generated from consumption across successive 10-min blocks within the same session

B6_cognitive.evidence: Operant task requires learned lever-press behavior; rats track price changes within session

B8_multivariate.evidence: Parameters analyzed via separate one-way ANOVAs; no dimensionality reduction

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water in chamber during session

D1_continuity.evidence: minimum of seven training days... Rats were tested in a pseudorandomized order with a dose-response curve... followed by combination tests

D3_recording_days.evidence: FR1 + FR3 training to stability + minimum 7 threshold training days + 3 stable sessions for stability criterion + multiple pseudorandomized test sessions (4 DOI doses + 2 M100907 combos) with intervening VEH

D4_baseline.evidence: VEH tests preceded each pharmacological challenge.

D5_followup.evidence: No recordings >=24 h after last drug

judge_notes: All three candidates identified two assays: FR5 cocaine IVSA and behavioral economics threshold procedure — kept as separate assays since they test different behavioural constructs (reinforcement vs. demand/motivation) with distinct protocols.
B1 for FR5: 4 distinct measures reported (infusions, active lever, inactive lever, latency) — scored 2 (4-6) consistent with qwen and gptoss over glm's 2-3.

B2 for behavioral economics: scored Yes since within-session demand curves are generated from sequential 10-min time blocks (qwen scored No, but glm/gptoss correctly identified temporal dynamics analysis).
D3 for behavioral economics: scored 15+ given >=7 training days on threshold procedure plus stability criterion plus 6 test sessions with intervening VEH days — likely >14 recording days.
